title: Detecting and Mitigating Subliminal Bias Transmission in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
summary: This paper proposes a framework to detect and mitigate subliminal bias transmission in multi-agent LLM systems by combining mechanistic interpretability with corpus-level constraints. The approach identifies bias-correlated neurons and applies constraint-based filtering to synthetic data, validated through generational bias amplification metrics on political news datasets.
gap: While ref-004 introduces a multi-agent LLM system for educational personalization, it does not address bias transmission in synthetic data. ref-010 and ref-012 demonstrate bias amplification in generational training and corpus-level mitigation, but do not integrate mechanistic interpretability for multi-agent systems. No existing work combines these methods to neutralize biases in multi-agent LLM-generated data.
approach: The approach implements a two-stage pipeline: (1) mechanistic analysis identifies neuron populations correlated with political bias (using regression tests from ref-010) and (2) corpus-level constraints (from ref-012) calibrate synthetic data during generation. Inputs are teacher model outputs; outputs are debiased student training datasets. The core differs from ref-012 by targeting multi-agent systems and using mechanistic insights to refine constraint weights, whereas ref-012 applies fixed constraints to single-model outputs.
evaluation: Evaluation uses ref-010's political news dataset to train student models on synthetic data generated by biased teacher agents. Bias amplification rates (percentage increase in right-leaning continuations) are measured across generations, comparing systems with/without mitigation. Baselines include unmodified multi-agent systems (ref-004) and ref-012's constraint-based method applied to single agents. Ablations isolate mechanistic analysis (neuron suppression alone) and corpus constraints (alone) to test their individual contributions.
